advices.diagnosis: The metrics show that OrderService is a classic god class: it has 26 public methods (NOM), a high cumulative cyclomatic complexity of 56 (WMC), and a cohesion score of 5 (LCOM4). The class also references four distinct internal collaborators (DCC=4) and has no private attributes (DAM=1.0). This indicates that the class is handling multiple responsibilities (order lifecycle, pricing, audit, notification) and is tightly coupled to several domain objects, which makes it hard to maintain, test, and evolve.

suggestions.title: Split OrderService into dedicated services
Move discount logic into DiscountPolicy

advices.risk_notes: Splitting the class will require extensive refactoring of the existing codebase and tests. The new services must be wired together by a composition root (e.g., a factory or dependency injection container). If the notifier is considered infrastructure, the NotificationService will still import it, potentially violating the layer rule; this can be mitigated by injecting an abstraction. The DiscountPolicy refactor may change the public API of PricingService, so callers that rely on the old discount methods must be updated. Finally, the overall DCC may not decrease if each new service still references the same collaborators; careful dependency inversion can mitigate this.
